tensions.name: Exported registry vs the only documented path: in-tree edits

side_a.position: A custom discovery plugin can be added out-of-tree: a downstream main() blank-imports a plugin package that init()-registers into llm-d-router's exported Registry, then calls runner.NewRunner().Run(ctx).
side_a.evidence: registry.go exports Registry (map[string]FactoryFunc) and Register(); main.go is only runner.NewRunner().Run(ctx); docs/discovery.md says to register the factory before Run(); PR #908 frames discovery backends as configuration-selected plugins.

side_b.position: In-tree extension is the documented path for SCHEDULING plugins and out-of-tree support is unratified: the filter tutorial edits runner.go's unexported registerInTreePlugins(); the Runner exposes no WithPlugins hook; Register() has no duplicate-type guard; no plugin call has panic recovery; and no downstream importer exists.
side_b.evidence: create_new_filter.md instructs in-tree registration; runner.go keeps registration unexported; issue #2105 (open, untriaged) lists 'in-tree plugins are the supported surface; out-of-tree plugins that panic take the process down' as an option; CONTRIBUTING.md is silent. Step-8 verification: pkg.go.dev reports 'No known importers' for cmd/epp/runner, pkg/epp/framework/interface/plugin and .../datalayer as of 2026-09-11 (verified with a second fetch provider and a raw request; GitHub code search hit a sign-in wall, so that avenue is a tool limitation, not evidence). Issue #2105 remains needs-triage with zero comments — 'at-your-own-risk' is one of three competing proposals, not ratified policy.

tensions.resolution: Side A wins, and more cleanly than the first reading suggested. Two separate documents were being conflated: create_new_filter.md's in-tree instruction is the tutorial for SCHEDULING filters, whereas the merged docs/discovery.md has an official 'Writing a custom discovery plugin' section that teaches exactly this mechanism — implement fwkdl.EndpointDiscovery, then fwkplugin.Register(PluginType, Factory) before Run(). So registering a custom DISCOVERY plugin is documented upstream, not merely tolerated; only the packaging detail (doing it from your own downstream main() rather than editing the repo) is an inference from cmd/epp/main.go's structure, and nothing blocks it: step-8 checks confirmed no internal/ path and no replace directives, at the cost of a go 1.26.6 floor and the controller-runtime dependency tree. The residual risks are real but bounded and identical for a fork: no duplicate-type guard (namespace your PluginType), no panic recovery anywhere in the framework (wrap Start() in your own recover(); issue #2105 is unresolved), and zero downstream precedent (pkg.go.dev shows no importers), which means you will be the first — pin a release, and run CI against upstream main. A fork adds rebase cost against a config surface that moved three times in four months and buys nothing in return.

tensions.name: Non-Kubernetes as first-class target vs on-ramp to Kubernetes

side_a.position: Upstream is committed to orchestrator-agnostic operation: GIE #1838 proposed a zero-Kubernetes mode because batch/RL customers (Mistral) asked for it; llm-d shipped EndpointDiscovery + FileDiscovery; PR #908 maintainers want K8s, file, Slurm and Ray discovery all as plugins.
side_a.evidence: GIE #1838 mode (1) 'static configuration of endpoints with zero dependency on k8s'; llm-d no-k8s blog: one routing stack, every platform; PR #908 maintainer quote; v0.8 'Beyond Kubernetes' release.

side_b.position: Non-Kubernetes mode is an adoption on-ramp and remains second-class: #1838's stated end goal is 'to land users on k8s'; a GIE maintainer called zero-k8s users out of scope for a kubernetes-sigs project; an agentgateway maintainer argued 'All Kubernetes or No Kubernetes — a hybrid is very odd'; every documented EPP HA mechanism is Kubernetes-coupled; Helm charts expose no discovery knobs; the no-k8s blog still calls Kubernetes 'the recommended choice' for production.
side_b.evidence: #1838: 'The end goal is to land users on k8s and the gateway api'; nirrozenbaum on mode (1); howardjohn on #620; docs/operations.md HA modes; charts README audited absence; no-k8s blog 'not a case against Kubernetes'.

tensions.resolution: Both are true at different layers, and the strategy should be built on that split: the ROUTING layer is genuinely platform-neutral and upstream-endorsed (the discovery abstraction won the #1838 debate — nirrozenbaum's 'add a discovery layer... similar to scheduler pluggability' is literally what shipped), but the OPERATIONS layer (HA, charts, CRD-driven policy, observability CRDs) is still Kubernetes-first. So bet on the discovery seam, and do not bet on upstream soon supplying non-k8s HA or packaging. Howardjohn's 'hybrid is odd' objection targeted EPP-in-k8s-without-Gateway-API for batch jobs; it does not bear on EPP-in-k8s-for-HA with non-pod backends, which is the hybrid this report recommends — flag it as an unconventional but mechanically supported shape.

tensions.name: Kubernetes-Lease HA vs Active-Active EPP off-cluster

side_a.position: Multi-replica EPP HA requires Kubernetes: the default Active-Passive mode uses coordination.k8s.io/Lease and all documented HA mechanisms are Kubernetes-coupled, so off-cluster you run one EPP or build coordination yourself.
side_a.evidence: docs/operations.md and the availability investigation (Lease leader election, StatefulSet priority routing, active-active deployment wiring); standby replicas answer NOT_SERVING during lease transitions.

side_b.position: Active-Active needs no leader election — a plain load balancer across N EPPs gives resilience 'without additional coordination' (v0.9), with near-linear scaling (1/2/3/4 replicas → 1.0/2.0/2.7/3.5x).
side_b.evidence: v0.9 blog on router HA; docs/operations.md Active-Active scaling table — but with warnings: flow-control state is per replica, and 'Active-Active mode should be avoided when using approximate prefix routing' because replicas do not share prefix state. Step-8 verification of the issue operations.md cites (#1290): it is a QPS/latency benchmarking issue, not a state-sync design doc — it never claims the precise-prefix index is partitioned and never names peer coordination as an Active-Active requirement. Its measurements point the other way: with precise prefix-cache routing at 500 QPS on real vLLM (Qwen2.5-7B), failures fall as replicas rise (1 replica: broken, 3,148 failures; 2: 57; 3: 31; 4: 18) and TTFT P50 drops from 165 ms to 30 ms. operations.md's Active-Active warning is scoped explicitly to APPROXIMATE prefix routing. Source reads add mechanism: cross_replica_syncer.go defines a separate opt-in CrossReplicaSyncer/CrossReplicaContributor surface, and the precise-prefix extractor implements only EndpointExtractor — so its cross-replica consistency comes from independent KV-event subscription, by design, not from a sync path.

tensions.resolution: Upgraded from inference to evidence-backed by the step-8 gap fetch. Off-cluster multi-replica HA is achievable as Active-Active behind a plain L4 load balancer, and precise (not approximate) prefix routing is what makes it safe: each replica independently subscribes to every endpoint's KV-event stream, so every replica converges on the same index without coordination — confirmed by code (the precise-prefix extractor pointedly does not implement CrossReplicaContributor) and by #1290's benchmark, where adding Active-Active replicas improved precise-prefix behaviour rather than degrading it. The Kubernetes coupling is real but narrower than first stated: it binds Active-PASSIVE leader election (coordination.k8s.io/Lease) and the only shipped peer-discovery plugin (PR #2501, k8s Pod-watch, still open) — though peer.go's own doc comment names file-based peer discovery as a first-class concept feeding the same sink, so a custom peer-discovery plugin is a sanctioned shape if cross-replica state is ever needed. Two operational cautions the draft must carry: the standalone Helm chart auto-injects --ha-enable-leader-election whenever replicas > 1, silently forcing Active-Passive unless disabled; and flow control stays per replica, so priority and fairness are enforced only within each replica's share of traffic. Remaining open gap: cross-replica session affinity was never evaluated (#1290 tested only independent synthetic requests), so session-pinned workloads should not assume Active-Active correctness.

tensions.name: 'Platform-invariant router' vs lost inputs and lifecycle off Kubernetes

side_a.position: The router behaves identically off Kubernetes: scoring, filtering, picking, saturation admission, FlowControl, P/D and metrics are unchanged, and precise prefix routing works with file discovery because it keys on Address:Port.
side_a.evidence: no-k8s blog and guide; docs/discovery.md ('All scheduling, request control, and metrics collection behaviour is unchanged'); precise-prefix extractor.go reading; FlowControl bands are static YAML.

side_b.position: Important inputs and all lifecycle guarantees are lost: InferenceObjective per-request priority, InferenceModelRewrite, k8s-notification-source and PodMonitor are inactive; readiness gating and dead-endpoint eviction become the caller's job; a dead backend keeps its datastore entry, ZMQ subscriber and KV-index entries until discovery deletes it; metadata updates only propagate on ≥ v0.9.0.
side_b.evidence: file-discovery README and discovery.md inactive-feature lists; llm-d no-k8s doc; issue #1403 (fixed PR #1404, v0.9.0); pod readiness semantics in discovery.md.

tensions.resolution: The invariance claim is true of routing LOGIC and false of routing INPUTS and LIFECYCLE; the report should say both without hedging. What the user must build is small and specific: a health-gated discovery source (only Upsert healthy endpoints, Delete promptly — this matters more than poll-vs-watch), a static priority plugin if priority tiers are needed, gateway-tier weighted canary, and Prometheus static/file SD. Pin llm-d-router ≥ v0.9.0. The load-bearing reason is that every 'lost' item traces to a controller-runtime reconciler or kubelet readiness, none to the scheduling code.

tensions.name: Fail-closed passthrough vs fail-open with fallback endpoints

side_a.position: Fail-open is standard: InferencePool failureMode FailOpen, Envoy ext_proc failure_mode_allow, llm-d's standalone Envoy preset ships router.proxy.failOpen for the lease-transition window, and the Endpoint Picker Protocol supports ordered fallback endpoints for retries.
side_a.evidence: InferencePool v1 spec; Envoy ext_proc docs; docs/operations.md standalone proxy; GIE PR #761 and protocol amendment PR #3003 (ordered endpoint lists); Envoy PR #38757 (dynamic_forwarding with fallback endpoints and a fallback LB policy).

side_b.position: Non-pod data paths are fail-closed by construction: the proxy has no endpoint list of its own to fall back to; agentgateway's standalone passthrough is deliberately fail-closed and fail-open remains an open issue; Envoy reviewers argued setUpstreamOverrideHost suffices and the multi-host retry design is still evolving.
side_b.evidence: agentgateway PRs #1429/#1658 and issue #1661; howardjohn: arbitrary passthrough 'breaks failOpen mode'; PR #38757 review thread.

tensions.resolution: For non-pod backends, fail-open is only meaningful if you configure an explicit fallback cluster; otherwise the honest default is fail-closed plus EPP HA (see the HA tension). Choose the proxy with this in mind: plain Envoy (llm-d's no-k8s reference config) lets you add a static fallback cluster and ext_proc failure_mode_allow deliberately; agentgateway passthrough is fail-closed until #1661 lands. Use the protocol's fallback-endpoint list for per-request retry resilience, which does not depend on EPP availability. Do not claim fail-open off-cluster by default — the no-k8s envoy.yaml's failure_mode_allow setting is unverified.

tensions.name: llm-d EPP vs alternative routers — and the protocol as the portable seam

side_a.position: Simpler routers are competitive or better off Kubernetes: vLLM Router reports 25% higher throughput and 1.2-2 s faster TTFT than llm-d, ships static worker URLs by default, and Dynamo/production-stack ship file or static discovery natively.
side_a.evidence: vLLM Router release blog (Llama 3.1 8B 8P/8D; DeepSeek V3 1P/1D); vLLM Router repo; Dynamo discovery backends; production-stack StaticServiceDiscovery.

side_b.position: llm-d's plugin depth (precise prefix, predicted latency, flow control, P/D profiles) is the asset, validated by large gains over round-robin; NVIDIA Dynamo ships its own EPP behind the same GIE Endpoint Picker Protocol, showing the protocol — not any one router binary — is the industry seam.
side_b.evidence: llm-d-reported 57x TTFT / 2x throughput vs round-robin; kv-cache-wins blog; Dynamo 'GAIE with vanilla vLLM' topology using a Dynamo EPP; GIE proposal 004.

tensions.resolution: Neither benchmark settles it: both are vendor-reported without published harnesses, and the vLLM Router comparison excluded vLLM's own DP coordinator and was produced with llm-d engineers' help. The decisive point for this user is different: because the proxy talks to any EPP through the same ext_proc protocol, the llm-d choice is reversible — the discovery customization is the only EPP-specific investment. Stay on llm-d for its scheduling depth, keep the proxy protocol-generic, and keep the discovery logic in a small, isolated plugin so switching EPP implementations later costs one plugin, not the architecture.

tensions.name: Official docs vs code at HEAD

side_a.position: Follow the published guidance: the no-k8s blog and guide, docs/discovery.md's custom-plugin skeleton, the plugin tutorial, and the v0.9 release blog describe how to run and extend the router off Kubernetes.
side_a.evidence: no-k8s blog/guide configs use dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef; discovery.md skeleton; create_new_filter.md; v0.9 blog: HA works 'without additional coordination'.

side_b.position: Trust the code: the discovery config key moved to dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef (PR #2434, 2026-08-25) with a legacy shim; the discovery.md skeleton does not compile against HEAD (value vs pointer receiver, missing Ready()); the router README never mentions discovery; llm-d.ai data-layer docs lag the repo; the v0.9 'no additional coordination' framing is inaccurate for the Lease-based default; a vault summary even misreported PR #1007 as merged.
side_b.evidence: PR #2434; runner.go resolveDiscovery; discovery.go (Ready()); source-analysis of the router README; docs/operations.md; custom-discovery investigator's GitHub API check of PR #1007. Step-8 verification: PR #2434 merged 2026-08-25, eight days AFTER the v0.10.0 tag (2026-08-17); no later release exists as of 2026-09-11, so the documented nested key ships in no release.

tensions.resolution: Code wins, with a process consequence for the strategy: this is a fast-moving, three-month-old interface whose docs trail its code by weeks. Use the shipped file plugin's plugin.go as the real template, pin a tagged llm-d-router release — and note that the nested `dataLayer.discovery.endpoints.pluginRef` key (PR #2434, merged 2026-08-25) is NOT in any release yet: v0.10.0 was tagged 2026-08-17 and is still the newest as of 2026-09-11, so a pinned v0.10.0 build uses the legacy `dataLayer.discovery.pluginRef`, run a scheduled CI job that compiles the plugin against upstream main, and read release notes for datalayer/discovery changes each cycle. The load-bearing reason is that three independent doc artifacts are already wrong about the exact seam this strategy depends on.
